frequency_question: What proportion of major federal agency regulatory actions requiring both a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking and a Final Rule achieve publication of the Final Rule within 301 days of initiating formal interagency review or initial drafting?
membership_rule: Includes all economically significant rules (impact >$100M) under the APA where a federal department published an NPRM and subsequently a Final Rule. Excludes emergency interim final rules that skip the standard NPRM stage.

cases.name: DHS USCIS Premium Processing Fee Adjustments (2020)
DHS USCIS Fee Schedule Final Rule (2024)

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 10 representative major immigration and fee-related rulemakings examined.
known_gaps: Varying complexity of economic analyses required for extreme fee changes ($100k+ fees are unprecedented and require extensive OMB OIRA review).
multiplier: 5 hits out of 10 sampled major DHS/labor rulemaking processes that completed the full NPRM-to-Final cycle within 10 months.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act timelines and standard OIRA review cycles remain legally mandated and stable over this horizon.
